newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish business group criticises govt spending.
newsitem.headline: Irish business group criticises govt spending.

text.p: The Chambers of Commerce of Ireland on Monday criticised the goverment's spending estimates for 1997 and called on finance minister Ruairi Quinn to reconsider next year's spending plans.
"Next year, the government is allowing for growth in current spending of some six percent -- three times the rate of inflation," the CCI said in a statement.
"Given the government's recent record in keeping its own promises, this is more likely to come to nine or 10 percent by the end of 1997," it said.
The CCI said that supply services spending is projected to show a net increase of 536 million punts in 1997, a six percent rise.

"If the government opted instead to stick to an increase in line with inflation, it would have saved 357 million or needed to collect that much less tax. This is a significant wasted opportunity," the CCI said.

It said it had no confidence in the government's ability to stick to its budgeted targets and the experience of recent years showed that the government's estimates on both spending and tax collection had been inadequate.

"The government continues to spend as if the punt is going out of fashion....The fiscal incontinence we have witnessed in recent years has not been remedied. Indeed, as an election looms, the condition appears to be worsen," the CCI said.
